content: Corex is a cough syrup that contains the active ingredients chlorpheniramine maleate and codeine phosphate. It is manufactured by a global pharmaceutical company and is available in countries such as India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and a few other South Asian nations. Corex is classified as a prescription medication, meaning it can only be legally purchased with a prescription from a licensed physician. Despite its prescription-only status, Corex is one of the most commonly available over-the-counter drugs in India. It is often used as an inexpensive and easily accessible substitute for codeine. However, studies indicate that over 90% of Corex sales occur without a valid prescription, highlighting significant regulatory challenges. Corex is not typically considered a fatal drug substitute unless consumed in extremely high doses. Nevertheless, it is associated with a range of side effects. Common adverse effects include short-term memory loss, insomnia, tremors, and muscle spasms. Users may also experience muscular pain and dehydration. Prolonged misuse of Corex can result in severe kidney damage. Additionally, Corex has a high sugar content, which may render it unsuitable for patients with acute diabetes. Its use should be carefully monitored in such individuals to avoid complications.
